teams.heading: Josua Tuisova returns as Ben Volavola starts at No. 10 for Fiji
teams.body: Jake White has recalled Josua Tuisova and Caleb Muntz for Fiji's Nations Championship test against Ireland in Dublin on Saturday, though Muntz starts on the bench. Ben Volavola takes the No. 10 jersey, partnering scrum-half Frank Lomani, and Peceli Yato captains the side from No. 8. Mesake Vocevoce drops from the second row into the back row, while Ponipate Loganimasi comes in at fullback. Tuisova lines up at first centre alongside Setareki Bituniyata.

lead.why: It is the only new Fiji-side team item in the pack, and it sets out the Fiji XV for Saturday's test.

teams.heading: Borthwick rings 10 changes for Japan, telling hopefuls to put team first
teams.body: England head coach Steve Borthwick has made 10 personnel and two positional changes for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Japan, handing starts to Will Joseph and Max Ojomoh. Borthwick says he is "really aware that the narrative around World Cup selection exists", but he insists the team must come first. Hopefuls have been warned not to go off script, with Henry Pollock starting at No 8 for a second time and only three players keeping their positions from the Australia win.

lead.why: It is the day's freshest England selection story, with a direct Borthwick quote on the World Cup pressure facing the squad.

teams.heading: Julien Marchand returns to start at hooker against Malcolm Marx
teams.body: Friday's Stade de France test will pit two of the world's best hookers against each other: France's Julien Marchand and South Africa's Malcolm Marx. Rugbyrama reports that Marchand is back in France's starting side, with head coach Fabien Galthié's team missing several key players. Former France captain Guilhem Guirado says the Springboks have plenty of effective jackalers, so Marchand's ability to steal ball may be almost vital, and he is eager to see how Marchand copes with South African clear-outs.

teams.heading: Beirne captains Ireland as Farrell names seven changes for Fiji
teams.body: Tadhg Beirne captains Ireland at the Aviva Stadium for the first time as Andy Farrell names seven changes for Saturday's Nations Championship match against Fiji. Beirne takes over from Dan Sheehan, who is out with concussion, while Mack Hansen moves to full-back and Jamison Gibson-Park returns to scrum-half after coming off the bench against Argentina. Ulster's James McNabney is named among the replacements and is in line to make his debut, and Nick Timoney shifts to number eight amid injuries to Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Sean Jansen.

lead.why: The confirmed Ireland team and captaincy is the freshest selection news, and it is not yet in any published edition.

teams.heading: Quesada names five changes to face Argentina, with Varney starting at scrum-half
teams.body: Head coach Gonzalo Quesada made five changes after the 7-66 defeat to South Africa: Allan moves to fullback, Varney starts at scrum-half and Fischetti returns at prop. The coach said some players arrived at camp not ready for 80 minutes, either after too much game time, as with Vintcent and Varney, or too little, as with Zuliani, so he picked a balanced side able to keep the pace. Argentina are missing Montoya, so Bautista Bernasconi starts at hooker, and Quesada expects the Pumas to come out aggressive from the first minute.

lead.why: Quesada's press conference is the day's freshest Italy news: the selection rationale behind five changes for the Argentina test.

teams.heading: Taine Basham starts at No. 8 as Aaron Wainwright is ruled out
teams.body: Aaron Wainwright picked up the minor calf injury against Japan and spent the week in a protective boot before being ruled out of Saturday's test against New Zealand. Taine Basham, recalled after impressing for Cardiff, replaces him, his first Test since the 2024 Six Nations. Wales head coach Steve Tandy said: "I'm delighted that Taine gets an opportunity this weekend." James Botham starts at blindside in place of Alex Mann, and Adam Beard returns to the second row.

lead.why: A new injury to a key forward, with the replacement selection that follows from it, is the freshest Wales team news in the pack.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi shuffles Pumas for Genoa, starting Bernasconi with Delguy at fullback
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi, Argentina head coach, has made five changes for Saturday's fifth-round Nations Championship test in Genoa. Bautista Bernasconi starts at hooker in place of the unavailable Julián Montoya, with Facundo Bosch on the bench, and Pablo Matera captains from No. 6. Juan Cruz Mallía's knee injury also reshapes the back line: Bautista Delguy moves to fullback, with Rodrigo Isgró on the wing.

teams.heading: Wallabies prop Angus Bell becomes first yellow-carded for hip drop tackle
teams.body: Wallabies prop Angus Bell was sin-binned after a television match official review on the first weekend of the Nations Championship. World Rugby formally outlawed the hip drop tackle on 1 November, so this window is the first in which referees have been asked to clamp down on it. Bell's tackle left England wing Immanuel Feyi-Waboso with an ankle injury that has ruled him out of England's remaining Nations Championship campaign. Australia's next assignment is Scotland at Murrayfield on Sunday.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie names Beauden Barrett captain for Wales test with eight changes
teams.body: Saturday's Principality Stadium test will mark Beauden Barrett's first start as New Zealand captain, his 149th cap, with brother Scott also starting at lock. New Zealand head coach Dave Rennie made eight starting changes from the side that beat Scotland 43-21, bringing Richie Mo'unga back at fly-half. Rennie said of Barrett: "Beauden brings such valuable experience and is massively respected by us all." Fehi Fineanganofo and Anton Segner make their first Test starts, and the bench carries six forwards, with Leicester Fainga'anuku named as back-row cover.

lead.why: A new All Blacks team announcement with a captaincy debut, a returning fly-half and an experimental bench, which a fan would talk about before Saturday's Test.

teams.heading: Springbok assistant coach Mzwandile Stick says Boks have prepared for Dupont-Lucu rotation
teams.body: Speaking on Thursday, Springbok assistant coach Mzwandile Stick said the team expects France's halfbacks to swap constantly, Antoine Dupont at 10 and Maxime Lucu at 9 rather than a conventional pairing. "It's not a fixed position. That's why it's going to be tricky," Stick added. He warned that giving the pair time and space would be punished, and said the world champions rely on their established rush defence rather than special plans built around Dupont.

lead.why: It is a new, South Africa-side coaching assessment of France's Dupont-Lucu halfback pairing, the main tactical question for the Boks.
